title: Persistent versus rectangular nuisance trajectory families

trajectory_families.law: Choose one p in {1/5,4/5} for the full episode; X1,X2 are conditionally iid Bernoulli(p).
Choose p1,p2 independently from {1/5,4/5} before their respective observations; conditionally independent Bernoulli observations.
Choose p1 first; after observing X1, choose p2(X1) from {1/5,4/5} using a public non-anticipating selector.

exact_implication: A terminal test calibrated for persistent shared nuisance is not automatically valid for a larger rectangular or history-adaptive trajectory family, even when every per-stage nuisance value comes from the same finite set.

implementation.scope: fixed two-stage counterexample and selector enumeration, not a generic dynamic nuisance model

required_receipt_semantics: nuisance scope: episode, device, channel, window, stage or observation
static, bounded-drift, Markov or history-adaptive transition semantics
whether transition choices are exogenous, action-dependent or public-history-dependent
calibration/reset effect on latent state and epoch
complete trajectory law/support, not per-observation marginals alone

validation.claim_boundary: The fixture proves that uncertainty-set geometry changes a test's error guarantee. It does not establish which trajectory-family semantics apply to a particular sensor; that requires traceable measurement evidence.
